name: inprocess-obi-tlul-timer-zipdma-f1f6
description: One OBI CPU with one real TL-UL rv_timer and a ZipDMA in one process: the timer carries the real F5 interrupt path and the DMA carries the RAM-to-RAM F6 path. F6 is runnable because the DMA control window is intercepted by the host and no DMA route to the TL-UL target is declared; a routed F6 is refused by name.
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex RVFI) reaches one TL-UL target at 0x40004000 and a ZipDMA control window at 0x40003000; the two windows do not overlap.

F1-F5 are the same declarations as configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-tlul-timer-f5.json: the timer behavior names the real interrupt output, INTR_STATE0 status, cause bit 0 and the compare-update clear.

F6 is a RAM-to-RAM four-word ZipDMA transfer: the host serves the DMA control word at 0x40003000 and the DMA master reads/writes RAM, so no target route is involved. A DMA route to the TL-UL timer is refused by name (unsupported-dma-route:apb3-target-only:tl-ul:tlultimer) because the route presents its beat on an APB3 request port.
The DMA completion interrupt is a second link in the same OR-ed CPU input; an F5 case still selects the timer link and an F6 case the DMA link.
This file declares the scenario; the run under runs/p0-1-ip/ is the evidence.
